item.title: Dollar edges higher against euro after U.S. inflation data
item.description: The U.S. dollar edged higher against major peers on Friday after closely watched inflation data showing higher consumer prices reinforced expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate increase next week.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: The U.S. dollar edged higher against major peers on Friday after closely watched inflation data showing higher consumer prices reinforced expectations of a Federal Reserve interest rate increase next week. Labor Department data showed that the U.S. consumer price index increased 0.4% in August after edging up 0.1% in July. In the 12 months through August, consumer inflation advanced 3.4% after rising by the same margin in July. The dollar rose broadly against the euro and Swiss franc before giving back some of those gains immediately after the data. The euro was down 0.07% at $1.1602. The dollar strengthened 0.2% to 0.814 against the Swiss franc.

item.title: Bonds, stocks selloff pauses as oil falls; pivotal CPI report due
item.description: A selloff in global bond and equity markets paused on Friday as oil prices retreated from a four-month high, though the recent surge in energy costs continued to fuel inflation worries and expectations that central banks may need to tighten policy.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Indyk, Stella Qiu
item.content:encoded: A selloff in global bond and equity markets paused on Friday as oil prices retreated from a four-month high, though the recent surge in energy costs continued to fuel inflation worries and expectations that central banks may need to tighten policy. Brent crude hit a four-month high of $109.97 a barrel on Friday after a 6% jump the day before, but it soon ran into selling pressure and was last down over 3.5% at $103.64. It was still set for a weekly rise of over 7.5%. Oil flows remained restricted through the Strait of Hormuz as the U.S. and Iran traded attacks , although prices have fallen after the Financial Times reported that foreign ministers in the Middle East were trying to work out a temporary deal to [USN:FWN4520ZF TEXT:"manage shipping"] through the waterway. But markets are still pricing in the risk of a protracted war. [USN:L6N45118W TEXT:"Comments"] from President Donald Trump that the conflict could last beyond the November midterm elections haven't helped, with bond yields surging globally on heightened inflation fears. "Markets are pricing in a scenario of higher rates for longer," said Gustav Helgesson, macro strategist at SEB. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was slightly lower on Friday at 4.94%, helped by retreating oil prices. It earlier touched its highest in almost three years at 4.979%. The 30-year yield scaled another 19-year top of 5.3836% before falling back to 5.352%. Bond yields move inversely with prices. The 2-year yield hit a new 14-month peak of 4.5961% after surging 12 bps on Thursday as markets ramped up bets that the U.S. Federal Reserve will have to raise interest rates this month to tame inflation, currently priced at about 67% probability. The selloff in the U.S. bond market on Thursday was partly due to a Treasury buyback programme that [USN:L6N452128 TEXT:"fell short"] of the expected $6 billion value. In Europe, the 10-year German Bund yield was up 1 bp for the day and up 17 bps for the week, its biggest weekly rise since March. EYES ON CPI The recent surge in oil prices has raised the stakes for August U.S. consumer price data due later in the day, which could make or break the case for a Fed rate hike next week. Forecasts are centred on a 0.2% monthly rise in the core measure of CPI, although risks are skewed towards a higher number as the [USN:L1N4500SJ TEXT:"PPI data"] overnight showed some stickiness. "Ahead of every payrolls print, every CPI print, it feels like it's the most important print yet, but it definitely feels like this one is," said SEB's Helgesson. "If we see a big divergence from expectations, we'll see very big market swings as well." Analysts at JPMorgan now expect eight of the nine developed-market central banks to hike interest rates by the year end, including the Fed, BOJ, all four central banks in Europe, and the reserve banks of Australia and New Zealand. "The tightening is for now expected to remain shallow, but risks to our forecasts lean in the direction of more action in the face of resilient growth, sticky core inflation, and commodity price pressures," they said in a note. The European Central Bank [USN:L1N452054 TEXT:"raised"] interest rates on Thursday for the second time this year and [USN:S8N42J013 TEXT:"some officials"] see more tightening ahead with October in play. RELIEF FOR EQUITIES European equity indexes took comfort from a dip in oil and gas prices although they were still set for sharp weekly falls. The pan-regional STOXX 600 (.STOXX) was up 0.6% on Friday but down 1.5% this week. Nasdaq and S&P 500 futures both rose about 0.6%. Asian stocks finished with sharp losses. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MIAPJ0000PUS) lost 1.5% while Japan's Nikkei (.N225) tumbled 1.9%. The U.S. dollar lifted with higher Treasury yields, having gained 0.4% on Thursday against its major peers. It was up 0.1% on Friday at 99.17. Gold rose 0.7% to $4,344 an ounce after dropping nearly 2% on Thursday.

item.title: 新興国向けプライベートクレジット、26年上半期は2倍超に
item.description:
Libby George
[ロンドン １０日 ロイター] - グローバル・プライベート・キャピタル・アソシエーション（...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
新興国向けプライベートクレジット、26年上半期は2倍超に 9:35 配信

ムンバイのスカイライン。2015年6月撮影。 REUTERS/Danish Siddiqui

Libby George

[ロンドン １０日 ロイター] - グローバル・プライベート・キャピタル・アソシエーション（ＧＰＣＡ）のデータによると、新興国向けプライベートクレジットに対する２０２６年上半期の投資額は８７億ドルと、前年同期の３６億ドルの２倍超となった。

ＧＰＣＡの調査担当マネージングディレクター、ジェフ・シュラピンスキー氏は、投資する年金基金、保険会社などの機関投資家について「成長市場、特にアジアをターゲットとしたプライベートクレジット戦略に対する有限責任パートナー（ＬＰ）の関心が続いている」として、力強い資金流入が今後も続く可能性があると強調。一方「インフレリスクの継続、貿易摩擦、地政学的紛争によって、世界的な信用情勢は不透明だ」と慎重な姿勢も示した。

ＧＰＣＡは約３００の民間の投資家から預かった総額２兆ドルの資産を運用している。ＧＰＣＡは２６年上半期の取引件数が２１５件、取引総額は６７億ドルと、前年同期の１１８億ドルから減った。２５年通年の取引件数は３７３件となり、年間の取引総額としては過去最高の２２５億ドルとなった。

一方、投資会社ナインティ・ワンは年末までに５億―１０億ドルの新興市場向けインフラ債務ファンドを立ち上げる計画だ。国際金融公社（ＩＦＣ）、アジアインフラ投資銀行（ＡＩＩＢ）、スウェーデンの政府系ファンド「スウェッドファンド」が出資することを既に表明している。

ナインティ・ワンのプライベート市場担当最高商業責任者（ＣＣＯ）のナズミーラ・ムーラ氏は、地政学的な変化によって米国からの分散投資が促進される中で、投資家は新興市場のリスクを再評価しているとの見解を示した。

オルタナティブ投資管理協会（ＡＩＭＡ）によると、プライベートクレジットは過去２０年間に拡大し、世界で３兆５０００億ドル規模に成長した。ただこのうち新興市場への投資は１割未満にとどまっている。

item.title: 中国新興ＡＩムーンショット、香港・上海の重複上場検討＝香港紙
item.description: [１０日 ロイター] - 中国の新興人工知能（ＡＩ）企業ムーンショットＡＩ（月之暗面）が資金調達と知名度向上を目指し...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
中国新興ＡＩムーンショット、香港・上海の重複上場検討＝香港紙 9:32 配信

ムーンショットのロゴ。5日撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[１０日 ロイター] - 中国の新興人工知能（ＡＩ）企業ムーンショットＡＩ（月之暗面）が資金調達と知名度向上を目指し、香港と上海での重複上場を検討していると、香港紙サウスチャイナ・モーニング・ポスト（ＳＣＭＰ）が１０日、事情に詳しい関係者２人の話として報じた。

それによると、大規模言語モデル「Ｋｉｍｉ」の開発元である同社は、香港での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）計画について出資者らと協議してきたほか、その後に中国本土で上場する可能性についても検討している。

上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け株式市場「科創板」を上場先とする公算が大きく、近く同取引所と協議を始める可能性があるという。

同紙は関係筋の話として、ムーンショットが中国本土での上場を検討しているのは、香港上場ＡＩ関連銘柄の株価が比較的低調なことや、香港でＩＰＯ案件が多数計画されていることを反映している可能性があると報じた。

ムーンショットのコメントは得られていない。

ロイターは先週、複数の関係者の話として、ムーンショットが香港で非公開でＩＰＯを申請したと報じた。

item.title: アンソロピック、「クロード」狙った中・ロ関連の悪用を阻止
item.description: [１０日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業のアンソロピックは１０日、過去８カ月間にわたり、同社のＡＩモデル「ク...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アンソロピック、「クロード」狙った中・ロ関連の悪用を阻止 9:29 配信

アンソロピックのロゴ。6月に撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[１０日 ロイター] - 米人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業のアンソロピックは１０日、過去８カ月間にわたり、同社のＡＩモデル「クロード」に対する複数の悪用事例を阻止したと発表した。これには、ロシア政府との関連が疑われるサイバースパイ活動や、クロードの機能を抽出・複製しようとしたと同社が指摘する中国ＡＩ企業の活動などが含まれる。

アンソロピックは最新の脅威インテリジェンスリポートの中で、サイバー犯罪者や国家が支援するハッカーが、単に作業を支援するだけでなく、サイバー攻撃の大部分を計画・実行するためにＡＩをますます活用していると指摘した。人間は多くの場合、実際に操作を行うのではなく、監督役として関与しているという。

リポートは「ＡＩの利用は、チャットボットによる単純な質疑応答にとどまらず、タスクを実行するマルチエージェント・フレームワークの活用にまで及んでいた」と分析した。

アンソロピックは、過去８カ月間に中国を拠点とする７つの研究所からの攻撃を阻止したと発表。これらには、テクノロジー大手のアリババ、ムーンショット、ディープシーク、シャオミなどが含まれていた。

同社によると、アリババと関連のあるオペレーターたちは、クロードの機能を抽出し、それをもとにアリババのＡＩモデル「Ｑｗｅｎ」を改良する目的で「最大規模の『違法な蒸留』攻撃」を実行した。アリババはコメント要請に直ちには回答しなかった。

アンソロピックは、今年５月から７月にかけて、アリババに起因すると見られる１億５１００万件以上の通信を検知した。これらは、同社が不正と見なした３５００以上のアカウントから発信され、１日あたり最大３００万件近くに達したという。

「蒸留（ディスティレーション）」とは、新しいＡＩモデルのトレーニングコストを削減するために、より大規模で高コストなモデルの出力を用いて、より小規模なＡＩモデルをトレーニングするプロセスを指す。

アンソロピックによると、チャットボット「Ｋｉｍｉ」の開発元であるムーンショットとディープシークは、一括クエリを実行するのではなく、機密情報を含むこともある顧客とのリアルタイムの会話をクロードに転送し、その応答を学習データとして利用していた。

このほか、アンソロピックは、ロシア拠点の脅威アクター「Midnight Blizzard」と手口が一致するハッカー集団が、ウクライナの政府、軍、外交部門の標的に対して、フィッシング、ホテルのＷｉ－Ｆｉ乗っ取り、米メタ傘下のメッセージアプリ「ワッツアップ」の乗っ取りを実行し、そのほぼ全ての段階でＡＩを利用していたと指摘した。

米政府は以前、「Ｍｉｄｎｉｇｈｔ Ｂｌｉｚｚａｒｄ」を、ロシアの対外情報機関ＳＶＲと関連付けていた。ワシントンのロシア大使館はコメント要請に応じていない。

アンソロピックはまた、クロードを悪用する「新たな種類の脅威アクター」を特定した。クロードを利用して「銃器、ミサイル、武装ドローン、爆弾、その他の兵器といった通常兵器用のソフトウエア、およびそれらを操作する照準・制御システムを開発する」者も含まれる。

同社のリポートには、中国、ロシア、イエメンにおいて、オペレーターがクロードを使用して兵器の設計・開発用ソフトを開発したり、兵器プログラムに関連する情報収集や調達を支援したりした事例が書かれている。

同社はまた、ここ数カ月で世界中の大手企業への攻撃に関与し、最も活発なサイバー犯罪組織の一つである「ＳｈｉｎｙＨｕｎｔｅｒｓ」の関連グループに結びつく活動を検知し、阻止したと明らかにした。

item.title: 金融業界向けチャットＧＰＴ、オープンＡＩが投資銀などに提供開始
item.description: [１０日 ロイター] - 米オープンＡＩは１０日、金融サービス業界向けに開発した対話型人工知能（ＡＩ）「チャットＧＰＴ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
金融業界向けチャットＧＰＴ、オープンＡＩが投資銀などに提供開始 9:25 配信

オープンＡＩのロゴ。6月撮影。 REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

[１０日 ロイター] - 米オープンＡＩは１０日、金融サービス業界向けに開発した対話型人工知能（ＡＩ）「チャットＧＰＴ」の提供を開始した。最新ＡＩモデルに、ＬＳＥＧやピッチブック、ダルーパなどが提供する金融データを組み合わせ、投資銀行部門のバンカーや株式アナリストの利用を想定している。

オープンＡＩのブログによると、「チャットＧＰＴ・フォー・ファイナンシャルサービシズ」は、モルガン・スタンレーとエバコアを設計パートナーとして開発された。

最新モデル「ＧＰＴ─６アストラ」を搭載しており、金融データツールを横断した情報検索、金融分野の推論、生成コンテンツの正確性を高めるよう構築されているという。複数の情報源をまたいだ調査、財務モデルの構築、自社テンプレートを使ったピッチブックなど顧客向け資料の作成が可能だという。

オープンＡＩは、同製品を通じて利用できる金融データの幅を拡充し、経験豊富なアナリストが従来担ってきた業務全般にわたって情報を識別・解釈・活用できるようモデルの学習をさらに進める方針を示した。

item.title: Houthis advance along Yemeni coast, threaten Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea
item.description: CAIRO: Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha on Thursday (Sep 10) and advanced down the Red Sea coast to strategic islands, military sources said, hours after President Donald Trump said he expected the Iran war
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Houthis advance along Yemeni coast, threaten Saudi oil exports in the Red Sea

Trucks explode as they burn during what the Houthis say was an attack targeting trucks coming from Saudi territory at Al-Wadiah border crossing near Al-Wadiah, on the Saudi-Yemen border, in this still image obtained from a handout video released Sep 7, 2026. (Photo: Houthi Media Centre/Handout via REUTERS)

CAIRO: Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port city of Mocha on Thursday (Sep 10) and advanced down the Red Sea coast to strategic islands, military sources said, hours after President Donald Trump said he expected the Iran war to end after the US midterm elections . Yemeni government military sources said the Houthis had gained further leverage over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait , the southern outlet of the Red Sea and one of the world's most important shipping routes, and had reached the islands of Hanish. If the Houthis were to gain control of the waterway on the opposite side of the Arabian Peninsula from the Strait of Hormuz, it could give their backer Iran a critical advantage in the war with the United States, reducing supplies through a second major transit corridor and sending oil prices surging. It could also make it harder for Trump to find an exit from a war that has hurt his Republican Party's electoral prospects ahead of the November midterms.

Yemen's Houthi-run humanitarian operations coordination centre said in a statement that Red Sea navigation is safe for all shipping companies except for Saudi vessels. Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, has relied on the Red Sea route since the Iran conflict effectively closed Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil used to flow. Yemeni government forces and their allies are relocating south along the Red Sea coast to Dhubab on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, across from Perim Island, government military sources said. Control of Dhubab and the island is key to gaining hold of the strait, they said. UN Special Envoy for Yemen Hans Grundberg told a UN Security Council meeting about Yemen on Thursday that the international community must act to address "a new and more dangerous phase" in the Yemen war. The Houthis' gaining control of Mocha gave them "a direct presence on the approaches to one of the world’s most vital straits", raising serious concerns about freedom of navigation, he said. Jenifer Neidhart de Ortiz, the US representative at the meeting, accused the Houthis of acting as "agents and tools of Iran". "This escalation is unacceptable, and those who enable it bear responsibility for its consequences," she said. Yemeni government, Iranian and regional sources told Reuters the Houthi advance down the coast this week came with direct guidance from Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps. Houthi spokesperson Mohammed Abdulsalam said, without elaborating, that the group's operations were defensive and would stop once attacks on Yemen stopped.

Related:

Trump says Iran war to end after US midterm elections, threatens to attack Pickaxe Mountain

Trump offers US$5,000 to every American if Republicans win midterm elections

OIL PRICES JUMP Brent crude prices jumped as much as 4 per cent on Thursday above US$105 a barrel on concern over disruption to supply routes, and the US national average price of diesel surpassed US$6 a gallon for the first time ever, according to price tracker GasBuddy. After joining the war with an attack on Israel in March, the Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia in July and escalated attacks this month. Tensions in the region remained high, with Saudi civil defence authorities issuing emergency alerts in the southwestern city of Khamis Mushait for the fourth time in 24 hours, as the Houthis attacked. Pakistan has delivered a Saudi warning to Iran to rein in the Houthis to try to prevent the crisis from spiralling, Saudi, Pakistani and Iranian sources said. A senior Iranian official said Tehran's response was: "Iran does not control the Houthis." The fighting comes during the biggest declared wave of US-Iran tit-for-tat attacks on Gulf shipping since the war began in late February. The US Treasury Department on Thursday announced new sanctions against firms and individuals aiding Hezbollah and other Iranian proxies as part of "Operation Economic Outcast", which aims to cut off Tehran's war funding.

Also read:

CNA Explains: With the Houthis' Red Sea threat, is the world running out of detours?

TRUMP SEES WAR ENDING AFTER MIDTERMS The war and subsequent increase in fuel prices have helped drive Trump's popularity to record lows, according to polls. He said Iran was trying to influence the midterm elections, which will determine whether his Republican Party retains control of Congress. "I think war is going to end immediately after the election because they can't hold out any longer. They're desperate to try and affect the election," Trump told reporters on Wednesday. Trump has previously set other deadlines for the war to end. In recent weeks, Washington had cited increasing success guiding tankers through the Strait of Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of global oil supplies before the war. But a resumption of fighting this month appears to have set back any such gradual reopening. Just seven vessels transited the strait on Wednesday, half the 10-day average, preliminary ship-tracking data showed. Iranian state media said on Thursday the Revolutionary Guards Navy had struck a US unmanned vessel at the entrance to Hormuz.

Source: Reuters/fh

item.title: Data centre upstarts evoke earlier broadband craze
item.description: While tech giants are leading the AI charge, independent operators like CoreWeave and IREN are playing a big part in building infrastructure. These ‘neoclouds’ have uncanny parallels with the alternative telecom operators which soared and then crashed as the millennium dawned.
item.dc:creator: Edward Chancellor
item.content:encoded: The data centres that run AI models can cost tens of billions of dollars to build. Most of this infrastructure is financed by deep-pocketed tech giants such as Microsoft (MSFT.O) and Amazon.com (AMZN.O) . Yet independent operators, known as neoclouds, are also playing an important role in the AI build out. Daniel Roberts, the co-CEO of data centre operator IREN (IREN.O) , claims the surge in capital spending is “fundamentally different” from past investment cycles. In fact, the AI is frenzy is reminiscent of the internet bubble; the neoclouds resemble the alternative telecoms firms that soared and crashed as the millennium dawned. By 2002, the telecoms industry in North America had spent nearly $500 billion over the preceding years building the broadband networks that were required in the internet era. Around half of this investment was made by alternative telecoms firms: upstarts taking on incumbent industry giants. Some of these so-called altnets built local telecoms systems to compete with the established “Baby Bells”; others invested in long-haul fibre-optic networks. Around 40 of the altnets were listed on U.S. stock exchanges. “Build it and they will come” was the industry’s boomtime mantra. The demand for broadband was deemed insatiable. Tech investment guru George Gilder forecast in early 2000 that data traffic would increase a thousandfold within five years. Enthusiasts believed that every dollar invested in new telecoms equipment would generate an incremental dollar of sales. The imminent arrival of new killer applications – one altnet CEO mooted holographic 3D video calls – would utilise the millions of miles of fibreoptic cable being laid. Between 1995 and 2000, the assets of the U.S. long-haul fibre operators – among them Global Crossing, Level 3 Communications and Williams Communications – expanded more than twenty-fold. Liabilities grew in tandem. Their businesses, however, remained stubbornly unprofitable. Projected demand for broadband turned out to be grossly exaggerated. As a result, the telecoms businesses were saddled with massive excess capacity. When the capital markets closed to telecom and technology companies in mid-2000, the altnets’ share prices collapsed, and several high-profile firms went bust. Some long-distance operators, including Global Crossing, faced scrutiny for using bogus capacity swaps to inflate revenue. Telecoms equipment firms like Lucent and Cisco Systems (CSCO.O) that had lent to the altnets were forced to write off their loans. Around 40% of high-yield telecoms bonds defaulted. Despite their public protestations of confidence, many telecom insiders bailed out long before the crisis arrived. Gary Winnick, the CEO of Global Crossing, raised more from sales of personal stock than his firm’s assets sold for in bankruptcy. While the altnets were mostly startups, many of today’s neoclouds were established to mine cryptocurrencies. CoreWeave, the largest of the group, started out in 2017 as Atlantic Crypto and entered the data centre business after the bitcoin crash of 2018. After the crypto market nosedived again in 2022, the launch of OpenAI’s ChatGPT chatbot in November of that year offered other crypto miners a lifeline. Their stocks of graphic processing units (GPUs) and contracted power agreements were indispensable for training and running the large language models that were now much in demand. While so-called hyperscalers such as Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Microsoft, Amazon, Meta Platforms (META.O) and Oracle (ORCL.N) account for around half of the sales leading AI chips made by Nvidia (NVDA.O) , neoclouds make up a sizeable share of the rest. The AI boom is “leading to the largest infrastructure buildout in human history,” declares Joshua Payne, the boss of Nscale, a London-based neocloud firm, which is spending tens of billions of dollars building a data centre in West Virginia. IREN’s David Roberts believes that each unit of new AI supply is bringing on multiple amounts of new demand. The “metric that defines success” in his business, says Roberts, is the number of GPUs you control. Nvidia’s chips are very expensive and large language models that are scaling up in pursuit of artificial general intelligence require them in ever greater quantities. That has left the neoclouds scrambling for cash. Several privately owned firms, including Nscale, Lambda, and Softbank-backed SB Energy, are preparing stock market listings. CoreWeave (CRWV.O) CEO Michael Intrator told CNBC earlier this year that the debt markets were dictating his company’s expansion strategy. At the end of June, CoreWeave’s total liabilities stood at $72 billion, an increase of 56% since the start of the year. Whereas the altnets financed themselves with high yield, payment-in-kind and zero-coupon bonds, neoclouds have been issuing bonds backed by GPUs and setting up special purpose vehicles with financial partners. Just as telecom equipment firms provided vendor-financing for their customers in the late 1990s, Nvidia plays a key role in supporting the neoclouds. The AI chip giant has invested directly in CoreWeave, Nscale, Nebius (NBIS.O) and others. Nvidia has committed to lease data centre capacity and provides a financial backstop for some neoclouds. It also has revenue-sharing agreements with a number of them. The investor Jim Chanos believes the neocloud business model is no more viable than the altnets of yesteryear. The famed short-seller argues their businesses don’t scale and lack any clear competitive advantages. Neoclouds are capital-intensive businesses that, in his financial model, cannot earn their cost of capital even when the depreciation schedule for their GPU chips is stretched out to 10 years. They should be viewed as equipment leasors that are dependent on a single vendor, Nvidia. Current bottlenecks restricting the construction of new data centres are unlikely to last. Chanos sees the sale of shares by CoreWeave insiders as a red flag. The alternative telecoms firms did not fail simply because they oversupplied a market whose demand projections were exaggerated. The industry was stricken with excess capacity in part because technological improvements massively increased the carrying capacity of installed fibre-optic networks. Neoclouds are also at the mercy of uncertain technological developments. Can Nvidia hold onto its position as the dominant maker of AI chips? Will OpenAI and its rival Anthropic – both of which are prime neocloud tenants - continue to dominate their field? Will the arrival of small language models that can run on local computers obviate the large language models and their expensive data centres? It is this profound uncertainty regarding the future of AI technology, rather than the level of capital spending, that makes the current boom “fundamentally different” from anything the world has seen before. WASHINGTON: The US government announced new sanctions on Thursday (Sep 10) against firms and individuals that it says are aiding Hezbollah and other Iranian proxies in the Middle East as it intensified its campaign to isolate Iran economically. The latest sanctions are part of the Treasury Department's "Operation Economic Outcast," first announced Aug 24, which aim to cut off the revenues that Tehran is using to fund the war, build missiles, conduct cyberattacks and support the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, or IRGC. Thursday's actions by Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control hit entities and individuals in Iraq, Lebanon and Turkey that Washington said supported Kata’ib Hezbollah, an Iraqi Shia paramilitary group under the command of the IRGC, and Hezbollah, a Lebanese Shia party, Treasury said in a statement. Treasury also announced a settlement with a US citizen who agreed to pay US$1.43 million to settle their potential civil liability for 39 apparent violations of sanctions on Iran, and issued a broad whistleblower appeal for tips on any sanctions evasion or money laundering by Iran.

Related:

OFAC also issued a bulletin making clear that it would deny most Iran-related licensing requests, except in exceptional circumstances, and said its licensing division had immediately begun denying "the vast majority" of outstanding Iran-related specific license requests. "OFAC will maintain this licensing policy until Iran changes its behavior, including obstructing the Strait of Hormuz, attacking US personnel and partners in the Gulf, and pursuing nuclear and conventional weapons," Treasury said. “Operation Economic Outcast is targeting those who continue to stand with the failing Iranian regime,” Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a statement. “Whether they finance terror, launder money, or help Iran evade sanctions, we will find them, cut them off from the U.S. financial system, and dismantle the networks keeping the regime afloat.”

item.title: Canada agrees on C$350 million air defense package for Ukraine, Carney says
item.description: Ukraine secures C$350 million from Canada for critical air defence interceptors as Kyiv runs low on Patriot missiles during intensified Russian attacks.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Canada agrees on C$350 million air defense package for Ukraine, Carney says

Ukraine secures C$350 million from Canada for critical air defence interceptors as Kyiv runs low on Patriot missiles during intensified Russian attacks.

Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney holds a bilateral meeting with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy during his visit to Calgary, Alberta, Canada, on Sep 10, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Todd Korol/Pool)

CALGARY, Alberta: Canada has agreed a C$350 million (US$253 million) aid package for Kyiv to acquire air defense interceptors, Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Thursday (Sep 10) after meeting Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. Kyiv is running critically low on US-made Patriot interceptors capable of stopping Russia's ballistic missiles at a time when Moscow is stepping up its attacks . "As Russia escalates its barbaric aerial warfare indiscriminately targeting civilian populations, Ukraine 's air defences are critical," Carney told reporters in Calgary. "Earlier today Canada and Ukraine finalised an agreement to deliver critical air defence interceptors...this C$350 million equipment package will help protect Ukraine 's people, infrastructure, and skies," he said.

He did not give details of which interceptors would be delivered or when the aid would start flowing. The weapons will be provided through a US program that allows third-party nations to quickly buy and supply weapons such as Patriot missiles to Ukraine .

Related:

"I thank you for this package. It's of (the) utmost importance, especially now," said Zelenskyy. Canada , one of Ukraine 's most vocal defenders, has committed more than C$25.5 billion in overall aid since Russia invaded in February 2022, including C$8.5 billion in military assistance. Carney also said Canada aimed to ramp up drone production to be able to produce millions of units within the next two years. A third of those would go to Ukraine , he said. Zelenskyy said Ukraine needed more technology and funding to produce enough drones to fend off mass Russian attacks. Canada is home to an estimated 1.3 to 1.4 million people of Ukrainian descent, forming one of the largest Ukrainian diasporas in the world. As part of the deals signed on Thursday, Canada will provide nearly C$435 million in new loan guarantees to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development to support energy security in Ukraine , especially during the winter.

item.title: Anthropic disrupts bioweapons research efforts, Russian hacking, Chinese Claude misuse
item.description: Anthropic broke up attempts to use its Claude models to develop biological weapons and carry out a suspected Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign against Ukraine, the AI heavyweight said.
item.dc:creator: A.J. Vicens, Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Anthropic broke up attempts to use its Claude models to develop biological weapons and carry out a suspected Russia-linked cyber espionage campaign against Ukraine, the AI heavyweight said in a report published on Thursday. It also accused Chinese competitors of hacking attempts aimed at extracting Claude's capabilities in its latest Threat Intelligence report, which documented malicious use of its technology over the past eight months. A growing number of [USN:L6N4520AE TEXT:"illegal hacking attempts"] by rogue AI agents along with concerns over the technology's risks voiced by industry insiders have increased the pressure on leading pioneers in the field, raising the [USN:L6N4520JB TEXT:"prospect of more regulation"]. Two Anthropic researchers warned this week that rapidly progressing artificial intelligence could lead to the extinction of the human race in the not-too-distant future. MISSILES, DRONES AND BIOLOGICAL WEAPONS In its report, Anthropic said it has long been a concern that AI models might one day reach the level of capability where they could help make existing pathogens more dangerous or create entirely new ones. It documented five examples of scientists using its models in ways that could support biological weapons development. In one case, a researcher in a region unsupported by Anthropic employed virtual private server infrastructure to access Claude and for weeks used it to plan avian influenza mammalian-adaptation experiments. Regions not supported by Anthropic include countries like Russia, China and North Korea among others. After detecting the misuse, it banned the accounts involved in such research and incorporated its findings into its frontier model safeguards, enforcement, and threat intelligence processes. Anthropic did not identify the institutions, the countries where they are based, or the specific biological agents and research techniques involved. It also identified what it called "new categories of threat actors" misusing Claude. That included using the platform to "develop software for conventional weapons, including firearms, missiles, armed drones, bombs, and other munitions, as well as the targeting and control systems that operate them." The report detailed incidents of operators in China, Russia and Yemen using Claude to develop software for weapons design and development, or to support intelligence gathering and procurement related to weapons programs. Rapid improvements in Anthropic's models have raised new risks, Jacob Klein, its head of threat intelligence, told Reuters. "A year ago, let's say you wanted to optimize a drone or optimize the software on a missile, the models just wouldn’t be as good at that task as they are now," he said. RUSSIAN HACKERS USE ANTHROPIC AI AGAINST UKRAINE OFFICIALS Anthropic found that cybercriminals and state-backed hackers were increasingly using AI to orchestrate and execute large portions of cyberattacks, with humans often serving as overseers rather than hands-on operators. "The use of AI went beyond simple questions and responses from a chatbot but rather involved the use of multi-agent frameworks," it said. One hacking group allegedly ran phishing, hotel Wi-Fi hijacking and WhatsApp-takeover operations against targets in the Ukrainian government, military and diplomatic sectors, using AI at nearly every stage, Anthropic said. The group's tradecraft was consistent with Russia-based threat actor Midnight Blizzard, which the U.S. government has previously linked to Russia's SVR foreign intelligence service. The Russian Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The group allegedly used AI to build a system that automatically detected when its malware was flagged by security defenses and rewrote the code until it evaded detection. Anthropic said it also detected and disrupted activity linked to affiliates of the ShinyHunters collective, currently among the most prolific cybercrime enterprises, which is linked to attacks on major corporations around the world. CHINESE AI LABS RUN ATTACKS TO EXTRACT CLAUDE CAPABILITIES Anthropic said it had disrupted attacks from seven China-based labs including Alibaba (9988.HK) , , Moonshot, DeepSeek and Xiaomi (1810.HK) during the period covered by the report. These companies did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Operators it linked to Alibaba ran what Anthropic called the largest "illicit distillation" attack, allegedly aimed at extracting the Claude models' capabilities and using them to improve the Chinese tech firm's Qwen models. Anthropic said it observed more than 151 million exchanges it attributed to Alibaba between May and July 2026, peaking at nearly 3 million per day from more than 3,500 accounts it described as fraudulent. Distillation refers to the process of training smaller AI models using output from larger, more expensive models in a bid to lower the costs of training a new AI tool. In another misuse of its technology, Anthropic said Kimi chatbot creator Moonshot and DeepSeek allegedly routed live customer conversations, which sometimes included sensitive information, through Claude and used its responses as training data. China's foreign ministry said it was not aware of the Anthropic report and that the government maintains that AI should be developed for good and opposes distortion of facts and smears against the country.

item.title: Trump handouts intensify economic Bermuda Triangle
item.description: The president promised voters $5,000 each if Republicans stay in power. Some $1 trln of new spending would exacerbate the Fed's inflation-fighting job and hamper Treasury's efforts to rein in deficits and bond yields. An increasingly dangerous policy vortex only vexes investors.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Rubin
item.content:encoded: Donald Trump will gladly pay Americans $5,000 each next year for their votes in November. The U.S. president's [USN:L1N45203G TEXT:"latest giveaway"], unveiled at a Republican gathering on Wednesday, lacks the $1 trillion of funding or any clear economic rationale. It befits the administration’s slapdash approach, but also exacerbates clashing agendas at the White House, Treasury Department and Federal Reserve in a murky Bermuda Triangle of policy that is increasingly unnerving investors. This week’s tumult epitomizes the relentless unpredictability. Trump escalated his trade fracas with Canada, eroding bilateral investment between neighbors and raising costs for vital industries such as auto manufacturing and agriculture. The unprompted war with Iran further spiraled into broader regional conflict, with new Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and U.S. bombing of Iranian oil tankers, which sent crude prices past $100 a barrel. A $6 billion buyback of Treasury bonds expanded the agency's vexing market [USN:L1N4510P7 TEXT:"intervention"] in the market. Moreover, the country's budget deficit is set to exceed $2 trillion this fiscal year, with federal debt surpassing the ignominious $40 trillion mark and 100% of GDP milestones. With plenty of high-grade corporate debt to buy, bond investors have been selling off Treasury bills, pushing 10-year yields beyond 4.8%. The producer price index, a measure of wholesale inflation before it reaches consumers, also has jumped sharply, with economists forecasting worse to come as costs for inputs, including diesel, stay high. The only unifying theme among these quandaries is that they are all at least partly self-inflicted. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's reactive bond buying muzzles the intended signals, with quickly rebounding yields eating away at his credibility. Trump’s fiscally dangerous new pledge to send out checks if his party retains congressional power after November's midterm elections evokes earlier empty promises. Where are the payouts from Elon Musk’s Department of Government Efficiency savings or the commander-in-chief's highly touted tariff dividends? This inscrutable mess probably leaves Fed Chair Kevin Warsh to try and steady the ship by [USN:SPN44V00M TEXT:"raising interest rates."] It would be an imperfect and incomplete step that also defies Trump's avowed desire for lower borrowing costs. It would be no mystery at all, however, if the economic vortex makes markets' faith disappear. Follow Gabriel Rubin on Bluesky and LinkedIn . President Donald Trump on September 9 proposed to pay every U.S. adult a $5,000 "Trump dividend" if Republicans keep control of Congress in the November midterm elections. The pledge came during the first day of a party convention being held in Dallas. The Treasury Department said on the same day that it would repurchase as much as $6 billion in 10- to 20-year U.S. bonds during a buyback operation on September 10, triple the amount of its last such operation. item.title: US defense is precariously stuck on 9/11
item.description: Even 25 years after al Qaeda attacks stunned the nation, its military runs on pricey and complex systems. Nimble and tech-savvy forces from Ukraine to Iran accentuate the obsolescence. A Cold War-era mindset and $900 bln budget reflect bad strategy based on outspending the enemy.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Rubin
item.content:encoded: Days after hijacked planes attacked the United States 25 years ago, Congress passed a $40 billion emergency spending package to fund recovery and an initial military response. One legislator, Democrat Dave Obey, caught a glimpse into the future: the law, he said, merely represented “a down payment” in a “nasty struggle.” It would indeed turn out to be a tiny upfront price for a quarter-century drain, and counting, on the country's coffers. President Donald Trump is using taxpayer money to fund a costly war in Iran that has reached crisis levels. Top military brass delivered a dire assessment to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth in recent weeks: extended conflict is unsustainable due to severe munitions shortages and overstretched troop deployments. Worse, an obsession with complex gadgetry keeps U.S. strategy stuck in a Cold War past. Before September 11, 2001, the United States was collecting peace dividends. The annual military budget was about $280 billion, or about $550 billion in today's dollars, amid a broad shutdown of overseas bases following the collapse of the Soviet Union. By last year, the tally exceeded $900 billion, more than twice as much as China after adjusting for labor costs and purchasing power. Before any new war-related increases, defense makes up half of all discretionary spending in an annual budget with a $2.1 trillion deficit. Any fiscal policy that tackles costs seriously will be up against this unsustainable growth. Since the bombing of Iran started in late February, the commander in chief has tried to cajole U.S. defense contractors into manufacturing more weapons, fast. In March, he convened executives from BAE Systems, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, RTX, Boeing, Honeywell Aerospace and L3Harris Technologies at the White House. Three months later, Trump issued a similar, more harried, request, which included the Pentagon pushing back on the industry’s optimistic production timelines. In [USN:L1N43G0TE TEXT:"July"], he traveled to Pennsylvania to twist arms again: “We have the best quality in the world, but we need a little more speed." As pricey missile orders pile up, modern technology is rapidly changing tactics on the ground and in the air. The U.S. military industrial complex faces another inflection point, just as it did in 2001, when blueprints and equipment from previous conflicts started becoming obsolete. Wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have provided live testing zones for cheap and nimble drone warfare. Asymmetric strategies that can shut down shipping lanes or paralyze economic activity are helping level battlefields with larger and wealthier adversaries, just as the 9/11 attacks did. These developments are quickly exposing the folly of Trump’s commitment to legacy systems like the F-35 fighter plane, a two-ocean Navy and full-scale revitalization of the U.S. nuclear weapons programs. It is slowing the broader reorientation to modern warfare. Two decades of war and military operations in Iraq, Afghanistan and beyond following 9/11 have cost more than $8 trillion, according to a Brown University tally . They include ongoing healthcare commitments to treat veterans and everyday "base budget" expenses that ran beyond $2 trillion through 2022. The Trump administration’s decision to remain at war, after promising to be a president who avoided them, led to a $1.5 trillion budget request for 2027, 50% more than for the previous year. It's an anachronistic approach that mortgages the country's future. For one thing, the United States is not getting enough literal bang for its buck. Although the weapons may be the most sophisticated and expensive ones on the planet, its adversaries are succeeding with cheap unmanned armies. For weeks when the latest Middle East siege began, U.S. and allied forces chased down thousands of Iran's Shahed drones, which cost an estimated $35,000 apiece, with Patriot missile interceptors that run about $4 million each. Such waste seems to be a feature, not a bug. For decades, the U.S. military has struggled with its advanced fighter jet program, the F-35. A joint production with approximately 2,000 defense contractors led by Lockheed Martin, the plane’s development has been “plagued by mounting costs and delays,” a 2024 government report said. It noted a “staggering" $2 trillion price tag over several decades. The math is getting worse, too: costly upgrades and maintenance have prompted the Air Force and Navy to cut down on overall flight hours for the crown jewel in their fleet. There’s plenty of demand for the F-35, but it increasingly features in broader debates. Spurned U.S. allies in the North Atlantic Treaty Organization are growing reluctant to buy American materiel. Moreover, Germany and Canada are among the countries to have raised concerns about the lethal jet being remotely controlled or otherwise influenced by U.S. authorities. The din grew loud enough that Lockheed and the Department of Defense formally denied the claims last year, but the supersonic aircraft will become less attractive to buyers as more cost-effective weaponry comes along and if diplomatic relations do not improve after Trump leaves office. Ukraine's war may prove instructive. Kyiv initially turned to German Leopard and U.S. Abrams tanks . The $10 million armored vehicles became top targets for Russian drones, however, and now serve a limited front-line role. The U.S. military is at least making some strides toward modern warfare. For 2027, the Pentagon asked for $70 billion to develop drones and counter-drone systems. It's spending billions to develop the Space Force, a sixth military branch started by Trump in 2019, and investing in satellites with contractors including SpaceX. At the same time, the budget calls for the creation of new “Trump class” battleships using expensive technology and decades-long procurement schedules. It could easily become the next F-35 boondoggle weighing down the pursuit of faster and cheaper weapons. Follow Gabriel Rubin on Bluesky and LinkedIn . September 11 marks the 25th anniversary of hijacked-plane attacks on the United States that killed nearly 3,000 people, brought down New York's World Trade Center and damaged the Pentagon. The U.S. Department of Defense is requesting a $1.5 trillion budget for 2027, a more than 50% increase over the previous year’s allocation, to fund Iran war operations, a major new shipbuilding campaign and heightened production to replace depleted missiles and other munitions caches. item.title: Japan signs first LNG emergency supply deal with Malaysia's Petronas
item.description: Japan signed its first deal to procure liquefied natural gas in an emergency with Malaysia's Petronas , Japan's industry ministry said on Friday, adding the country would seek similar agreements with other countries.
item.dc:creator: Yuka Obayashi, Emily Chow
item.content:encoded: Japan signed its first deal to procure liquefied natural gas in an emergency with Malaysia's Petronas (PGAS.KL) , Japan's industry ministry said on Friday, adding the country would seek similar agreements with other countries. The master sales and purchase agreement would enable Petronas to deliver LNG to the Japan Organization for Metals and Energy Security, which would in turn supply private buyers, such as utilities, if they were unable to obtain it elsewhere. Speaking at a press conference after the LNG Producer-Consumer Conference in Tokyo, Tetsuya Azuma, a director of the Japanese ministry's energy resources development division, did not give further details, such as the volume or contract length. Petronas Executive Vice President and CEO of gas & maritime business, Datuk Adif Zulkifli, said the deal reflected the trust built up with JOGMEC "over many years". "By establishing a more agile framework for future LNG supply arrangements, we are better positioned to respond to evolving energy needs and contribute to greater supply resilience," he said in a statement. Japan also signed a memorandum of cooperation with Montenegro on energy projects, including developing an LNG receiving terminal and gas-fired power plant. The outline deal builds on a memorandum of understanding JERA, Japan's largest power generation company, signed last year with the Montenegrin government to explore the development of an LNG terminal and an associated gas-fired plant in the country. Azuma said the new memorandum aimed to support private-sector initiatives to help expand the global market and further Japan's efforts to diversify sources of LNG supply.

item.title: OFRBS Summary
item.description: L'Europe rebondit malgré le ton ferme de la BCE, Wall Street attentive à l'inflation
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Europe rebondit malgré le ton ferme de la BCE, Wall Street attentive à l'inflation 11 septembre (Reuters) - Wall Street est attendue en hausse et les Bourses européennes rebondissent vendredi à mi-séance, les actions regagnant un peu de terrain au lendemain d'une nouvelle flambée des rendements obligataires, dans un contexte de craintes d'un resserrement monétaire plus agressif de la part des banques centrales face à l'inflation. La France divise par deux, à 0,5%, sa prévision de croissance pour 2026 PARIS, 11 septembre (Reuters) - Le gouvernement français a abaissé pour la troisième fois cette année sa prévision de croissance pour 2026, la ramenant à 0,5% contre 0,7% en juillet et 1,0% initialement, a annoncé vendredi le ministre de l'Economie Roland Lescure. France: L'économie n'est pas dans un état catastrophique, mais il faut réduire le déficit, selon Moulin L'économie française n'est pas dans une situation catastrophique mais le gouvernement doit agir pour réduire le déficit public du pays, a déclaré vendredi Emmanuel Moulin, le gouverneur de la Banque de France (BdF). Auto: Les USA et le reste du monde divergent clairement, selon Stellantis Le directeur général de Stellantis, Antonio Filosa, a souligné jeudi soir au cours d'une conférence d'analystes l'ampleur de la divergence actuelle au sein des marchés automobiles mondiaux, entre les Etats-Unis et partout ailleurs. Alstom signe des contrats pour €1,2 md pour des trains à batterie en GB Alstom a annoncé vendredi avoir signé avec TransPennine Express des contrats d'une valeur de 1,2 milliard d'euros pour la fourniture et la maintenance à long terme d’une flotte de trains électriques à batterie en Grande-Bretagne. BCE-Une nouvelle hausse des taux pourrait intervenir dès octobre, selon des sources Les responsables de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) prévoient un nouveau resserrement de la politique monétaire dans les mois à venir pour lutter contre l'inflation en zone euro et pourraient prendre de nouvelles mesures dès octobre, ont déclaré deux sources à Reuters. La BCE relève à nouveau ses taux d'intérêt, l'inflation persiste La Banque centrale européenne (BCE) a, comme prévu, relevé jeudi ses taux directeurs pour la deuxième fois cette année, la poursuite du conflit au Moyen-Orient menaçant de maintenir l'inflation au-dessus de l'objectif pendant une période plus longue. Renault va produire en Argentine un nouveau pick-up pour accélérer hors d'Europe Renault Group a dévoilé jeudi un nouveau pick-up, nommé Niagara et doté d'une silhouette peu courante dans la panoplie du constructeur automobile français mais indispensable pour réussir en Amérique latine, une région clé pour sa stratégie de croissance hors d'Europe. AB Foods: Primark va proposer un service de livraison à domicile au Royaume-Uni Associated British Foods a annoncé jeudi que sa branche de vêtements Primark, dont elle prévoit la scission l'année prochaine, proposera bientôt un service de livraison à domicile au Royaume-Uni. Eutelsat commande 229 satellites à Airbus pour renforcer son réseau OneWeb L'opérateur franco-britannique Eutelsat a annoncé jeudi qu'il allait renouveler et étendre son réseau OneWeb jusqu'en 2034 après la signature d'un accord avec Airbus portant sur 229 satellites supplémentaires en orbite terrestre basse.
